MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  FEBRUARY 21, 2023

1.  CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. and was held via
  teleconference pursuant to Senate Bill 361.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Brown Schachter, Boothe, Combs, Munday,
  Nash*, Persichina**, Romanelli,

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Martin, Varner

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Public Works Director
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

* Left the meeting at 7:28 p.m.
** Left the meeting at 8:00 p.m.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, AUGUST 30,
  2022.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
ROMANELLI to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  AUGUST 30, 2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A. DEEP VALLEY DRIVE - DRYBANK DRIVE TO SILVER SPUR ROAD ALL-WAY STOP
  ANALYSIS AT ROXCOVE DRIVE AND PEDESTRIAN VOLUME COUNT REVIEW.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. This item
involved taking data counts at the pedestrian crossing on Deep Valley Drive at Roxcove Drive.
Surveillance video was gathered, and an overview of the collision history was provided.

Director Wahba stated that repaving has been held off until the 927 Deep Valley Drive project has
been completed; this is a good time to look at street crossing improvements. He stated that the
Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, February 21, 2023
 issue at this intersection (Deep Valley Drive/Roxcove) is that the Brickwalk does not have enough
parking and people dropping off at Kumon prefer to park in the adjacent lots or on the street. He
asked if a 3-way stop is warranted at this time, and if not, how the crosswalk can be better
addressed.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that this intersection was reviewed for an all-way stop
according to the guidelines in the California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices; various
criteria are involved, however this location does not meet the guidelines due to low vehicle
volumes. A stop sign would not be recommended on Deep Valley Drive at Roxcove Drive.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that this intersection as well as the mid-block location
west of Roxcove Drive, and the round-a-bout at Drybank Drive are locations proposed to be
considered for the Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) grant application. She also
added that consideration of bulb-outs, and more traffic counts will be done if the HSIP grant is
awarded.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that this item was precipitated by general speed
concerns and requests from businesses, including Kumon Tutoring Center and Reverent Coffee
Shop, for a crosswalk. He stated that he observed eight pedestrians crossing between 5:53 –
5:59 p.m. today. He stated that there is a crosswalk behind the roundabout that is not convenient
and the next one is blocks away.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER asked if the traffic collision report from 2017 to 2018 was prior to
Kumon and Reverent. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki confirmed that this is correct.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACTHER stated that she agrees with COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY
and something should be done at the mid-block to facilitate crossing.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS inquired about the location of the crosswalk and asked about
view obstructions. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated a bulb out would be considered as
well as additional red curbs in order to help with visibility. COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS also
expressed his concern with visibility at night.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety
Committee discuss the items presented and receive public testimony. Staff does not recommend
the installation of an all way stop at Deep Valley Drive and Roxcove Drive at this time. Staff does
recommend some enforcement of parking regulations and pedestrian crossings by the Sheriff’s
along Deep Valley Drive as practical or as requested by business and residents and to review the
library and tutoring center as part of the HSIP grant application, which may be awarded to the
City within the next month or so.

Public comment was invited. No public comment was received.

Director Wahba suggested that the recommendation to the City Council could be to go ahead and
obtain a proposal from Willdan to go ahead and start putting together some design for a crosswalk
closer to the 627 building and the library and then also looking at some improvements to the
existing crosswalk on Deep Valley Drive at Roxcove Drive. Also, the possibility of designing for
bulb outs at the crosswalks and the consideration of in-pavement flashers.
Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided an explanation on the various factors required to
install a crosswalk, and agrees that there is a need to do something at this location.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, February 21, 2023
 COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MUNDAY,
  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL THAT THE CITY MOVE
  FORWARD WITH THE DESIGN OF A LIRBARY CROSSWALK IF THE CITY IS
  AWARDED THE HSIP GRANT; AS PART OF THE GRANT, CONSIDER THE
  INSTALLATION OF IN-ROADWAY WARNING LIGHTS AT THE ROXCOVE DRIVE
  CROSSWALK.

There being no objection, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER so ordered.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER inquired about Willdan’s recommendation for Sheriff’s
Department enforcement for those parking in the red zones. Director Wahba stated that he can
request that the Sheriff’s Department do enforcement in the area.

B. MASONGATE DRIVE - SPEEDING CONCERN NEAR FERNCREEK TRAIL CROSSING.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. Staff
received an e-mail from Terry Griggs regarding an encounter that she had with a truck that almost
did not stop for the equestrians. Data was collected that showed the average daily traffic volume
over 2 days on Masongate is about 646 vehicles; most vehicles are traveling between 21 and 30
mph. There was one reported collision in 2017, 100 feet north of Masongate.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided suggestions including: moving the trail warning sign
closer to the roadway, making the sign larger; installing a “trail crossing ahead” sign prior to the
trail warning sign; installing triangle limit yield lines; installing a rapid rectangular flashing beacon
(RRFB) that is triggered by a button that is pushed by equestrians or pedestrians; and changing
the color of the sign from yellow to fluorescent green.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the committee discuss the
concerns on Masongate including the equestrian crossing, take public testimony, and provide
direction to staff regarding the matter.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that the RRFB would be helpful in having people stop
since the button needs to be pushed before crossing. Also, she commented that she liked the
idea of changing the color of the sign from yellow to green. She also agreed that the existing sign
should be moved closer to the roadway.

Alexis Neilson, Resident on Sugarhill Drive, stated that she likes the suggestions that would help
with the visibility for the equestrians; however, as a parent to young children, she is concerned
with the speeding cars. Since there are no sidewalks, many people walk on the street and the
speed of vehicles going up or down hill on Masongate is concerning. She stated that the staff
report noted that the grade on Masongate close to Stagecoach is too steep for a speed hump,
but asked that it be explored further since the grade drops significantly when you pass
Stagecoach.

J. Ged, Resident, stated that this incident happened due to a distracted driver, which can happen
anywhere. She stated that more signage would not have helped this situation since it was just the
driver not paying attention. She stated that in her opinion adding additional signage is going to
make the street look cluttered.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, February 21, 2023
 Terry Griggs, Resident, stated that in her analysis the problem seems to be that people are picking
up speed when driving down Masongate; she asked about the possibility of adding a stop sign at
Stagecoach. She also stated that neighbors’ hedges need to be cut back in order for equestrians
to be able to see the cars coming down the hill.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE responded to Ms. Neilson’s commented in regard to speed
humps and recalls that 50% plus one of the neighborhood needs to vote in favor; she stated that
she has spoken to neighbors who are not in favor of speed humps in the neighborhood. She
added that based on the average speed, a different plan of action would be helpful. There is an
issue of safety in that area.

Susan Robinson, Larga Vista Resident, commented that the neighborhood does not have
sidewalks or street lights, which she likes; however, she believes the speed limit, which is 25 mph
in the neighborhood is too high. She asked why the speed limits could not be lowered or have
signs where the speed limit is 15 mph when children or horses are present. She also commented
that asking the Sheriff’s to cite for speeding or yielding to pedestrians would be helpful.

Administrative Analyst Corea acknowledged that an e-comment was received from Michael
Stone, Resident on Stagecoach Drive, who also had concerns with speeding vehicles.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS stated that he agreed with relocating the sign.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked if it would be possible for the curb bulb out to provide a
sanctuary for horses and pedestrians, as well as cause cars to slow down as the street narrows.
Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated it is something that could be considered.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER commented that she lives on Ranchview, and the installation of
flashing in-roadway lights has improved the crossing in the area. Due to her own experience, she
stated that the RRFB that can be activated by the rider or pedestrian is valuable.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that a single incident has raised a broad concern
about speeding and he can attest that the same issue is happening on Silver Saddle Lane. He
stated that what they have done is asked Mike Goldsmith, the City’s Maintenance Superintendent,
to put up the speed board in their neighborhood. The speed board flashes if the car is exceeding
the speed limit and suggested that this may be something to consider.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER asked if the RRFB would be solar powered. Traffic Engineering
Deputy Itagaki confirmed that it would be solar powered.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE commented that she liked the idea of bulb outs for equestrians
and pedestrians, but stated that there may be a concern with drainage. Director Wahba confirmed
that drainage would make this a costly solution. His suggestion would be to begin with the
changes to sign and consider installing the RRFB.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS
to,
  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO RELOCATE THE EXISTING
  NORTHBOUND TRAIL WARNING SIGN CLOSER TO THE ROADWAY; INCREASE THE
  SIZE OF THE TRAIL WARNING SIGNS FOR BOTH DIRECTIONS OF TRAVEL; CONSIDER
  USING FLUORESCENT YELLOW GREEN SIGN COLOR FOR TRAIL SIGNS; CONSIDER
  INSTALLATION OF SOLAR POWERED RRFB AT THE TRAIL CROSSING.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  4
Minutes, February 21, 2023
 AYES: BROWN SCHACHTER, BOOTHE, COMBS, MUNDAY, ROMANELLI
NOES:
ABSENT: MARTIN, NASH, PERSICHINA, VARNER
ABSTAIN:

C. PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST NEAR CHANDLER RANCH ROAD - SPEEDING CONCERN.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. She
stated the residents of Rolling Hills Country Club Owners Association are concerned with
speeding on Palos Verdes Drive East near Chandler Ranch Road. The data that was collected
showed that some cars are driving very fast. She added that there are visibility concerns at this
location as well. She suggested the installation of additional speed limit signs and possibly
installing a flashing beacon with those signs; or the installation of an LED outline speed limit signs;
or the installation of radar speed limit sign. She stated that staff recommends that the committee
discuss the item and provide direction to staff regarding this matter.

Bill Hagelstein, President, The Residences at Rolling Hills Country Club HOA, stated that aside
from speed, there is also concern with visibility. He explained that there are many vehicles coming
in and out at this intersection, especially when there are events at the Rolling Hills Country Club,
and it is difficult to see cars coming down the road. He also stated that if anything, the speed limit
in this area should be 35 mph not 40 mph. Mr. Hagelstein stated anything the City can do is
greatly appreciated.
In response to a question by CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Mr. Hagelstein stated that a solar
powered illuminated sign that shows the required speed limit and also the current speed of the
driver would be helpful to make this location safer.
BB Wang, Homeowner at The Residences, stated that in a perfect world, she would walk her kids
to school; however, the road is scary for her. She stated that the radar speed feedback sign would
be great. She asked if there was a solution for the poor visibility when driving out of the
neighborhood, such as reflective mirrors where you can see left and right since the road is at a
bend.
Administrative Analyst Corea acknowledged that eComments were received earlier and
forwarded to the committee.
CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER asked if the installation of the speed radar signs would be in both
directions. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that it could be either, and they would be
installed prior to approaching Chandler Ranch Road.
CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER commented that the “Intersection Ahead” sign would work to alert
the drivers on southbound side of the road. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the
reason she chose the sign with the two side streets is for Bridlewood Circle.
COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS asked if staff could ask the Sheriff’s Department for data on how
much enforcement has been done at this location and how many citations have been issued.
Director Wahba stated that staff can request that information and request that they do
enforcement as well.
COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked if the speed limit was assessed after the construction
was completed. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the most recent engineering and

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  5
Minutes, February 21, 2023
 traffic survey for the city was done in 2021 (whereby about two-thirds of the project was complete).
She also provided an explanation of how speed limits are determined and posted.
COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that she agrees with the recommendation of adding
speed limit signs as well as the radar speed feedback signs. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
stated that both can be done.
COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that there is vegetation on the west side of Palos
Verdes Drive East which may be causing a view obstruction. He suggested that removing or
trimming the vegetation significantly may give the driver’s better visibility. Traffic Engineering
Deputy stated that this has been looked and explained that the limit line was moved forward in
order to provide more visibility. Director Wahba added that a portion of the three-rail fence was
also removed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked if it is possible to make the striping more apparent where
you have a sanctuary to pull into and then wait to merge. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated
that this could be looked into.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated the there is a refuge at Ranchview Road and explained
how it could be problematic due to the speed.

Mr. Hagelstein clarified that this is not a vegetation issue and stated that the fence contributes
greatly to the lack of visibility along with the curvature of the turn. He also stated that the Sheriff’
Department write a lot of tickets for speeding in this area.
COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI asked if removing a rail would solve the issue. Mr.
Hagelstein stated that it would not solve the problem because it is a visibility combination of both
the three-rail fence and speed.
In response to a question by Director Wahba, Mr. Hagelstein confirmed that the fencing to the
north is an issue and clarified that as you exit Chandler Ranch Road and attempt to make a left,
the fence on the right causes a visibility issue. Director Wahba stated that one or two more
sections can be removed, beyond what was already removed about three years ago.
Ms. Wang stated that when exiting onto Palos Verdes Drive East and looking left, the visibility at
the turn lane that comes into the Chandler Ranch Road and looking right, the three-rail fence
vertical poles are an issue. She believes the main issue is speed.
Director Wahba stated that the radar speed signs and adding more speed limit signs on both
sides are good suggestions. Also considering a solar powered flashing light around the sign
warning of a split intersection is also a good idea.
COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS
to,
  APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF MORE SPEED LIMIT SIGNS ALONG PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST; INSTALLATION OF AN “INTERSECTION” AHEAD SIGN WITH
  A FLASHING BEACON ON THE SOUTHBOUND LANE; AND INSTALLATION OF A
  SOLAR RADAR SPEED FEEDBACK SIGN FOR THE NORTHBOUND DIRECTION OF
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST.

AYES: BROWN SCHACHTER, BOOTHE, COMBS, MUNDAY, ROMANELLI
NOES:
ABSENT: MARTIN, NASH, PERSICHINA, VARNER
Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  6
Minutes, February 21, 2023
 ABSTAIN:

D. PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST - PEDESTRIAN
  CROSSING CONCERNS.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. She
stated that this item was received from several residents concerned with students crossing Palos
Verdes Drive North at Palos Verdes Drive East.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS suggested installing a “no turn on red” sign on the southwest
corner of Palos Verdes Drive North when turning right onto Palos Verdes Drive East. Traffic
Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that it would increase delay on Palos Verdes Drive North
particularly due to the lane onto Hitching Post Drive.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER asked about “no turn on red” during designated times. Traffic
Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that it may be helpful to limit to minimal times while providing
pedestrians this relief.

Susan Robinson, Resident, stated that the issue is with the drivers who are making a right-hand
turn from Palos Verdes Drive North onto Palos Verdes Drive East without stopping for the red
light. She shared an incident with a vehicle while she had stepped off a curb and expressed her
concern for the safety of children who are crossing this intersection. She added that when crossing
Palos Verdes Drive North from Dapplegray Park to George F Canyon, it’s difficult for drivers
making a right-hand turn to see pedestrians.

Lynne Yen, Resident, stated that she bikes her child to school every morning and afternoon; she
expressed her concern for children, some of whom are on electric bikes, and their safety. She
stated that sometimes truck drivers do not see her at her height, and she is concerned for the
safety of children. She stated that the “no turn on red” restriction would increase safety. She stated
that the issue is in all directions.

Ashling Grigorian, Resident, stated that she is trying to reestablish the walking school bus due to
the traffic congestion caused by the elementary and high schools starting at the same time (8:30
a.m.). A lot of parents are concerned with this intersection. She began walking her kids to school
and noticed that almost no one stops when making the right-hand turn. She added that they are
trying to get fifty children for the walking school bus to alleviate traffic on Palos Verdes Drive
North; but need safe walking conditions for their children.

Katherine Stapleton, Resident, asked if better coloring and visibility could be added on the
crosswalks. She also asked about a flashing signal for turning only, and about a “right turn only”
sign.

M. Sawoya, Resident, stated that both of her boy’s ride to school every day. She and her boys
have nearly been hit crossing the street at this intersection. She stated that vehicles do not stop
for the red light and her and five other parents stand in the middle of the road to make sure kids
cross safely. She stated that she has a younger child who will need to walk across this street next
year and she is afraid for his safety. She also stated that a “no turn on red” from 7:30 a.m. – 8:30
a.m. and 2:00 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. would make parents feel safer.

Ms. Robinson asked about having the Sheriff’s Department cite people at this intersection.
Director Wahba stated that he can make this request.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  7
Minutes, February 21, 2023
 COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that on Palos Verdes Drive North in front of City Hall
west of Crenshaw Blvd. there is a median where pedestrians can stop and cross in two segments.
He suggested doing a similar crossing on Palos Verdes Drive North, west of Hitching Post Drive.
COMMITTEE MEMBERS expressed that this could be problematic.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS stated that this is a significant issue and stated that adding a
“no turn on red” during restricted hours would be beneficial at the southwest corner of Palos
Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE agreed with the “no turn on red”. She asked for the possibility
of adding a green arrow when it is safe to make the right turn. She also expressed concern that
there is no crossing guard at this intersection.

Director Wahba stated that he recalls that this committee has discussed a crossing guard at this
intersection in the past.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she will need to look into the possibility of adding a
green arrow due to the age of the signal poles. She thinks that a good starting point is the “no
turn on red” sign and enforcement. Typically, when new signs are installed; flags are put up to
provide notice of them. Director Wahba added that the size of the sign needs to be legible
considering the large width of the intersection. Also, there will be two signs; one on the far side
across the street and one closer to the drivers. Traffic Engineering Deputy suggested that the
time restriction be from 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked about the possibility of a crossing guard. Traffic
Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the number of pedestrians crossing does not meet the
criteria for a crossing guard.

COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MUNDAY,

  RECOMMENDING THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF “NO
  RIGHT TURN ON RED” SIGN FOR EASTBOUND RIGHT TURNS AT PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST FOR A PARTICULAR TIME PERIOD.
  CITY STAFF AND CITY COUNCIL TO DETERMINE THE RESTRICTED TIME PERIOD; AND
  REQUEST SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT TO CONDUCT EDUCATING ENFORCEMENT
  REGARDING THE NEW SIGN POSTING.

AYES: BROWN SCHACHTER, BOOTHE, COMBS, MUNDAY, ROMANELLI
NOES:
ABSENT: MARTIN, NASH, PERSICHINA, VARNER
ABSTAIN:

E. REQUEST FOR GREEN-COLORED BIKE LANE

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. She
stated that this item was received from Ms. Katie Stapleton to consider green pavement markings
on bike lanes to improve visibility of cyclists. She provided examples of the various green bike
lane options.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  8
Minutes, February 21, 2023
 Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety
Committee discuss this item and provide direction to staff regarding the use of green-color
pavement bike lanes.

She added that the city is looking to do a bike lane on Palos Verdes Drive East in the southbound
direction with parallel parking.

Katie Stapleton, Resident, stated that she is requesting that the bike lanes become more visible
in Rolling Hills Estates and on the Palos Verdes Peninsula due to the number of accidents that
have occurred, herself included. She stated that the green-colored bike lanes would protect
cyclists and reduce fatalities.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI asked if there is a possibility that CalTrans may adopt this
concept and be mandated in the city. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that CalTrans has
already adopted the use of the green pavement markings; however, it is not generally required.
She stated that when restriping and there is a bike lane, cities may be required to follow the new
standard.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE, Traffic Engineering Deputy
Itagaki stated that this is not just paint and actually similar to a slurry seal. Director Wahba asked
if it has a texture and reflectivity. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that it does have a
texture but is not sure about the reflective coating.

In response to a question by CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
stated that it could be costly but there is an option of only doing the markings as opposed to the
entire bike lane. She added that one challenge is the amount of gutters along the bike lanes,
which are part of the bike lanes, that would need to also be green.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
BOOTHE,

  TO RECOMMEND THAT STAFF RETURN TO THE TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE
  WITH CONCEPTUAL EXAMPLE AND COST ESTIMATE FOR GREEN-COLORED BIKE
  LANE INSTALLATION.

There being no objection, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER so ordered.

7.  STAFF ITEMS
